## Bug: ship skill release script fails on `set -o pipefail` under dash

**Severity:** critical (release workflow broken — work items not closed, changelog empty)
**Status:** FIXED — see commit `e80fca0f` (work item `LP-0MSQ0NTMO00577UJ`, 2026-08-19)

## Fix summary

All `set -o pipefail` commands in ship skill scripts are now wrapped in `bash -c` to ensure they run under bash (not dash):

- `check-audit-gate.js` `getCandidateItems()` — wraps query in `bash -c`
- `check-final-validation.js` `getCompletedOrInReviewItems()` — wraps query in `bash -c`
- `release/generate-changelog.js` — wraps query in `bash -c`
- `release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` — uses `#!/usr/bin/env bash` shebang

## Regression tests

- `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs` — verifies `bash -c` wrapper
- `tests/unit/test-generate-changelog-query.mjs` — verifies `bash -c` wrapper

## Original acceptance criteria (all met by the fix)

1. ✅ Release scripts never invoke `set -o pipefail` through a shell that doesn't support it — all wrapped in `bash -c`
2. ✅ Grep audit confirms no remaining bare `set -o pipefail` via /bin/sh
3. ✅ `getCandidateItems()` returns real in_review items on dash systems
4. ✅ Regression tests exercise the pipefail-portability fix
5. ✅ Unit tests added covering the fix
6. ✅ Comments document the portability requirement

## Original description (for reference)

When execSync runs `set -o pipefail` commands through /bin/sh on dash systems, the shell exits with "set: Illegal option -o pipefail". This caused CHANGELOG.md to contain 0 work items and no work items were closed after release v0.1.14.
data.title: Ship skill: 'set -o pipefail' fails under /bin/sh (dash) — breaks work-item close + changelog steps during release

# Bug: audit false-positive screen crashes with "Argument list too long" on large ruff finding sets

## Problem Statement

The audit skill's false-positive screen (`_screen_ruff_findings` in `audit_runner.py`) batches ALL ruff findings from the code-quality scan into a single Pi call. When the scan produces a very large finding set, the OS rejects the process spawn with `[Errno 7] Argument list too long: 'pi'` and the entire screen fails.

## Observed Failure

- Auditing LP-0MSISZS1O004KJRR (llm project) on 2026-08-18: ruff scan produced 1,600+ findings, almost all `invalid-syntax`/E7xx in `start-llama.sh` (a long bash script linted as Python).
- The screen crashed: `Warning: false-positive screen failed unexpectedly: [Errno 7] Argument list too long: 'pi' — all findings defaulted to uncertain (caution-first).`
- Consequence: no findings were classified, no tracking chores could be created, and the whole run degraded — the item was left blocked with 1,600+ untracked `uncertain` findings. The audit had to be completed manually.

## Impact

- **Critical audits can fail entirely** whenever the changed-file scope contains a file that triggers hundreds/thousands of ruff findings (e.g. a bash script linted as Python, or a generated file).
- Findings default to `uncertain` → they stay blocking with "candidate false positive — producer decision required" annotations, or in the crash case, no items are created at all.
- Manual intervention required for every such audit; the audit pipeline is not robust to large finding sets.

## Users & User Stories

- **Auditor/operator:** "When I audit a work item whose changed files trigger many lint findings, the false-positive screen should still complete — I shouldn't have to manually re-run the audit because the batch was too large."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No crash on large finding sets:** The false-positive screen completes (or degrades gracefully per-finding) when the ruff scan produces 1,000+ findings — no `Argument list too long` crash.
2. **Chunked or bounded batching:** Findings are sent to the model in bounded batches (e.g. max N findings per Pi call, configurable) instead of one unbounded argument list, OR the screen degrades to a documented per-finding fallback that still creates tracking chores.
3. **No untracked findings:** A screen failure (of any kind) never leaves findings completely untracked — either classified, or tracked as candidate false positives, or reported with a clear count in the audit report.
4. **Regression test:** A test covers the large-finding-set path (e.g. simulated 2,000-finding scan) verifying the screen does not crash.
5. **Full audit test suite passes** after the change.

## Constraints

- Must not reduce the caution-first default (a failed screen still defaults every finding to `uncertain`, never `confident-false-positive`).
- Must not change the audit verdict semantics — only the batching/transport of findings to the model.
- Backward compatible with existing audit runs and persisted reports.

## Existing State

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_screen_ruff_findings` builds one Pi invocation with all findings inline; the OS `execve` fails with E2BIG ("Argument list too long") when the payload exceeds ARG_MAX.
- The screen is skipped entirely (zero Pi calls) when the scan yields no ruff findings; non-ruff findings are never sent to it.
- Discovery source: audit of LP-0MSISZS1O004KJRR (llm project), 2026-08-18, discovered-from LP-0MSISZS1O004KJRR.
data.title: Bug: audit false-positive screen crashes with Argument list too long on large ruff finding sets

# Pi extension: mirror proxy-side compaction into client dispatch context

Client-side consumer of the proxy compaction signal. A single Pi extension
(`pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/`) that reads the proxy's compaction
response headers and mirrors the proxy's compacted view in the client's
*dispatch* layer only — the session JSONL (storage) is never modified, so
pre-compaction messages remain fully recoverable via `/tree`, `/fork`,
`/export`.

Producer side: proxy work item LP-0MTYGZ1DI0004QP8 (surface compaction
metadata via response headers: `X-Compaction-Occurred`,
`X-Compaction-Marker`, `X-Compaction-Turns-Summarized`,
`X-Compaction-Recent-Turns-Kept`).

## Wire contract (frozen by LP-0MTYGZ1DI0004QP8)

Emitted only when live compaction is applied, on both buffered and streaming
(`StreamingResponse`/SSE) responses:

| Header | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `X-Compaction-Occurred` | `true`; the other three are emitted with it |
| `X-Compaction-Marker` | **base64** of the exact message content the proxy injected, including the `_SUMMARY_MARKER` / `_SUMMARY_MARKER_END` delimiters |
| `X-Compaction-Turns-Summarized` | decimal integer — folded middle turns |
| `X-Compaction-Recent-Turns-Kept` | decimal integer — retained tail turns |

Contract rules the extension MUST honour:

- The marker header is **base64-encoded**. The extension base64-decodes it
  to obtain the verbatim marker message content; it never constructs,
  reformats, or guesses marker text (including delimiters).
- `X-Compaction-Occurred: true` is the only trigger. Non-compaction responses
  (noop / below-trigger / dry-run / `remote_with_guidance`) carry **none** of
  these headers.
- Absent headers mean "no new signal" — they do **not** clear previously
  captured in-memory state. Mirroring continues until the session ends or the
  client restarts (the proxy re-signals once after a restart, then the view
  is stable).
- Header emission is fail-safe and additive: the proxy never changes dispatch
  behaviour to produce them, so the extension treats missing or malformed
  headers as a no-op (pass the original context through unchanged).

## User Story

As a Pi user whose sessions are compacted by the LLM proxy, I want the
client to send the same compacted history the proxy already stored, so
the proxy resumes INCREMENTAL compaction instead of re-summarizing from
scratch on every turn — while my full session history stays intact on
disk. As an operator, I want zero changes to Pi internals (extension
file only).

## Design

Storage/dispatch separation:
- STORAGE (session JSONL): never touched by the extension. Grows
  forever — that is the intended source of truth.
- DISPATCH (per-turn context): reshaped via the `context` event to
  `[system, first_user, proxy_marker, recent...]`.

Handlers:
1. `after_provider_response`: fires after the HTTP response is received and
   *before* the stream body is consumed, so headers are available for SSE
   responses too. Read `event.headers`, base64-decode the marker, capture the
   turn counts, and keep a per-session in-memory state (NOT persisted — on
   client restart the proxy re-signals and re-compacts once, then stable).
2. `context`: if compaction state exists, rebuild the dispatched list —
   head (system + first user message) + decoded proxy marker (verbatim,
   never constructed by the extension) + recent tail, respecting turn
   boundaries (user/assistant/toolResult groups not split).

Pi's own `/compact` setting (on/off) is irrelevant to correctness.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Extension loads via pi's extension discovery mechanism (repo
  convention: source under `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/`, symlinked
  into `~/.pi/agent/extensions/` exactly like `pi-client/proxy-sse-signals`);
  harmless no-op when proxy compaction headers are absent (normal sessions
  unchanged).
- AC2: After a compaction-signalled response, the next dispatched context
  contains the base64-decoded proxy marker content (verbatim, including
  delimiters) and excludes the folded middle turns; the tail matches
  `X-Compaction-Recent-Turns-Kept` without splitting turns, and the number of
  excluded middle turns is consistent with `X-Compaction-Turns-Summarized`.
- AC3: Session JSONL is unchanged across a full compaction cycle — no
  append/rewrite by the extension (verified by diffing the file before and
  after).
- AC4: Pi's own compaction setting (enabled/disabled) does not affect
  correctness.
- AC5: `/tree`, `/fork`, `/export` still expose the full pre-compaction
  history after the cycle.
- AC6: The extension never constructs or guesses the marker text; it comes
  only from the base64-decoded proxy header.
- AC7: Tests or a documented manual verification script cover: no-header
  passthrough, header → mirrored dispatch, marker base64 round-trip,
  tail-boundary handling, JSONL immutability, malformed-header no-op.
- AC8: Header names/values are validated against the proxy-side unit tests
  (LP-0MTYGZ1DI0004QP8) — four exact header names, `X-Compaction-Occurred:
  true`, base64 marker round-trip, decimal counts; the coupling point is
  documented.

## Notes / related

- **Critical path**: this is the sole client-side consumer of the compaction
  bridge; without it the proxy's compacted view and Pi's dispatched view stay
  divergent (history_mismatch fallbacks and CREATION re-summarization every
  turn).
- Depends on the proxy response-header contract defined in
  LP-0MTYGZ1DI0004QP8.
- External dependency: the Pi coding agent extension event model
  (`after_provider_response`, `context`) — no Pi source modifications.
  Verified against the pi extension docs: `after_provider_response` exposes
  normalized `event.headers` before stream consumption; `context` may return
  `{ messages }` to reshape what is dispatched.
- Risk: pi docs note "Header availability depends on provider and transport.
  Providers that abstract HTTP responses may not expose headers." Validate
  that the Local Proxy provider path exposes response headers before relying
  on the last two ACs; if it does not, this item is blocked and the contract
  needs a sidecar channel.
- Header size caveat (from LP-0MTYGZ1DI0004QP8): summaries are base64'd into
  a single header; if real summaries exceed a few KB, revisit with a sidecar
  endpoint (`GET /sessions/<id>/compaction`).
data.title: Pi extension: mirror proxy-side compaction into client dispatch context
